title: When the Current Turns
premise: Zephyrine Sandoval has spent seven years drifting between dig sites, outrunning the shadow of her famous archaeologist mother, Dr. Imelda Sandoval, whose expedition upriver to a sunken colonial galleon has gone silent. When the salvage fleet of corrupt magnate Aurelio Vance moves in to strip the wreck, Zephyrine realizes her mother's last radio message was meant for her alone, containing coordinates and a confession about the artifact that made the family name. Racing six tides upriver with a disgraced river pilot and her mother's estranged first mate, she uncovers that the 'discovery' was stolen from a drowned river community, and that her mother stayed behind to protect it. In the flooded hold, Zephyrine must choose between salvaging her inheritance or returning the treasure to its rightful keepers, ending with her broadcasting the truth on the very frequency her mother once used, finally claiming an identity of her own making.
about_author: Mara Sterling is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping tributaries before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who measure their lives in water levels rather than calendars.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Working a contract dig in a coastal marsh town, she measures her life in distances traveled, refusing calls from her mother's foundation. A telegram arrives: the upriver expedition has missed three scheduled check-ins. Emotional beat: the ache of chosen exile meeting the pull of blood.

chapters.title: The Silent Frequency
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. She tunes into the expedition's old radio band and hears only static, then a garbled fragment of her mother's voice saying coordinates and one word: 'return.' She books passage on a mail steamer against every instinct to run. Emotional beat: fear disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. At the river port of Puerto Cobre she learns the tide schedule: six tides until the salvage fleet's dredges can enter the gorge. She meets Cass Ibarra, a river pilot stripped of his license by Vance's lawyers, who knows the back channels. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance over shared enemies.

chapters.title: What the Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV, flashback woven through present. Packing her mother's old field kit, she finds a journal page torn out, and remembers childhood summers when Imelda hid maps from funders. Emotional beat: realizing her mother was always more complicated than the legend.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Clock
chapters.summary: Cass POV. He pilots the battered boat Mariposa into the gorge while Zephyrine reads current lines better than he does, grudging respect forming. They pass the first salvage scout boat anchored suspiciously far downstream. Emotional beat: two loners discovering complementary skills.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. They shelter at San Remedios, a half-submerged village whose people were displaced decades ago when the river was dammed for Vance's interests. An elder recognizes the Sandoval name and spits. Emotional beat: shame of inherited privilege surfacing.

chapters.title: Radio Ghosts
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. From the village's old transmitter she picks up a repeating signal: her mother's voice, pre-recorded, giving a bearing that shifts each night. Someone is still sending it. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into dread—her mother may be alive, or someone is using her voice as bait.

chapters.title: Vance's Wake
chapters.summary: Cass POV. The salvage fleet's lead ship, the Aurelia, overtakes them, and aboard it Zephyrine spots Tomás Reyes, her mother's first mate, working for Vance. Betrayal stings until she notices him signaling them covertly. Emotional beat: the vertigo of not knowing who is enemy or ally.

chapters.title: The Gorge Passage
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. A night run through the narrows, using tide timing Cass swears is impossible; Zephyrine's surveyor instincts save them from a rock shelf. The Mariposa limps through with a cracked hull seam. Emotional beat: trust forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Camp of the Missing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. They find the expedition's base camp abandoned mid-meal, radios smashed, but a fresh grave marked with Imelda's compass. Zephyrine refuses to believe it. Emotional beat: grief denied, anger ignited.

chapters.title: Tomás in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Tomás POV. He slips away from the Aurelia at night and finds them, confessing: Vance coerced him after the discovery, but Imelda faked her own disappearance to draw the fleet away from the true site. The grave is empty. Emotional beat: relief curdling into new urgency.

chapters.title: The Stolen Find
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Tomás reveals the galleon's cargo includes the Sandoval Codex—the artifact that built the family reputation—which Imelda actually recovered years earlier from San Remedios' flooded church and never disclosed. Emotional beat: the inheritance myth collapsing.

chapters.title: Tide Three
chapters.summary: Cass POV. With three tides left, they plan to reach the wreck's true location inside a submerged cavern system the fleet's sonar can't read. The village elders offer guides, softening toward Zephyrine as she vows restitution. Emotional beat: justice reframed as repair, not revenge.

chapters.title: Diving the Old Church
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. First dive into the flooded nave where the codex was originally found; she experiences her mother's discovery from the other side, understanding why Imelda couldn't hand it to Vance. Emotional beat: empathy replacing resentment.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. The Aurelia's patrol catches their surface support; Cass is taken, and Vance offers Zephyrine a partnership: her name legitimizes his claim, and her mother walks free. Emotional beat: temptation of the easy bargain.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Feigning acceptance, she gets aboard the Aurelia, locates Cass, and learns Vance already has divers in the cavern. She sabotages the dredge winches during a shift change. Emotional beat: choosing principle over safety.

chapters.title: Flooded Hold
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Tide five. She dives the cavern ahead of Vance's crew and finds Imelda alive in an air pocket, injured, guarding the codex. Their reunion is fierce and wordless—seven years compressed into shared breath. Emotional beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: Tide Six
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The final tide: Vance's divers close in as the cavern begins to silt. Tomás turns the Aurelia's searchlights to blind his own employers; Cass threads the Mariposa into the cavern mouth for extraction. Emotional beat: everyone paying their debt at once.

chapters.title: The Current Turns
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Climax: a surge tide floods the lower gallery; Vance, refusing to release the codex case, is caught by the collapse. Zephyrine saves his diver instead, letting the river take the gold but not the man. Emotional beat: mercy as victory.

chapters.title: What Was Never Ours
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Aftermath in San Remedios: the codex is formally returned to the village, and Imelda publicly signs over her claim. Mother and daughter argue, then laugh, then sit in silence that no longer hurts. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as responsibility.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. From the village transmitter, she broadcasts the full account of the theft and return on her mother's old frequency, naming names, including her own family's. Vance faces inquiry; Cass regains his license. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Miles Ahead
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV, closing. She and Cass take the repaired Mariposa downriver toward a new survey contract—hers, under her own name, no Sandoval attached. She stops counting miles and starts counting mornings. Emotional beat: identity claimed, journey open-ended.
